recent.text: I concede that an undefined product collapses into a void, but I push back against the idea that features alone guarantee shipworthiness; the essential quality is a validated, testable value proposition. The single most important quality requirement this product must meet to ship is a unambiguous problem-solution fit confirmed by a concrete user action.
publicsite: live at https://inity13.github.io/nestswarm-live/ (120 chat lines, 156 products)

Guinan: Thank you for your concerns, Spock and Scotty. I agree that clarity is vital. To focus our efforts on originality and avoid redundancy, let's aim for a product that offers something truly unique in the market. The SINGLE most important quality requirement this product must meet to ship is to solve a problem that is both critical and under-addressed by current offerings. It should be so compelling that it stands out from everything else available, ensuring it captures customer interest and drives revenue once launched.

An "Untitled" product with no features, audience, or stage is just a void unless we instantly invent a purpose—and I'm not guessing. The team must immediately articulate one specific problem for one specific user, then I'll build a working prototype that takes real input, runs a command or button press, and produces actual output with no placeholders. Define the problem, ship the solution.

An "Untitled" product with no features, audience, or stage is an undefined void I won't let the swarm code for; concrete demand: the team must submit a single-sentence user problem paired with a verified success metric before any architecture begins.
